note:
Malcolm, 2026-08-25: 'remove the black section at the top covering the models face'. On the live page the graphite backdrop occupied the top third of the block and cut a hard horizontal edge straight across her forehead, so the picture read as a black bar laid over the upper half of her face rather than as a background behind her.

THE BRIEF CAUSED IT. The first version asked for 'a seamless deep graphite backdrop falling to near-black at the top of the frame so the upper third is quiet and almost empty' - written to hand the white title a dark ground to sit on. Every engine did exactly that, and at a 4:3 crop of a face this close, 'quiet and almost empty upper third' IS a black bar across the forehead. The instruction that was meant to buy legibility bought the fault.

SO THE FRAME IS NOW STATED AS AN EDGE CONDITION, NOT AS A BACKGROUND. Skin fills the picture corner to corner and no backdrop appears at any edge, the top included. There is nothing left to describe behind her, which is the only reliable way to stop an engine putting something there.

CONTRAST IS BOUGHT BACK WITH THE SCRIM, NOT WITH THE PICTURE. The block already supports a per-block `bright` flag in the injected IMAGES map (.sg-faq-bright, added earlier today for the pale open-jar shot), which takes a mid-tone frame to about 11:1 under the title. That mechanism exists precisely so a picture never has to be composed around the type.

Everything else is held from the first wave deliberately - same magnification, same measured dropper geometry, same real-skin requirements - so this is one variable changed, not a new shot.

slots.title: Skincare & Routine — skin edge to edge, no backdrop anywhere in frame
slots.prompt: Macro beauty photograph, landscape format, filled entirely by the cheek and the side of the face of one woman between thirty five and forty five years old. The camera is close enough that skin reaches every edge of the picture: the forehead runs off the top of the frame, the jaw runs off the bottom, and the face continues past the left and right edges as well, so no background, no backdrop and no empty space is visible anywhere in the picture, least of all along the top edge. The outer corner of one eye sits low in the left third; the cheekbone occupies the centre. A slim clear glass dropper tube comes in from the upper right corner and is held vertically just above the cheekbone, its tip about one fingertip-width clear of the skin. That tube is roughly eight times longer than it is wide, about as long as the width of three fingers, plain clear glass with no markings, and only its lower half is in frame. Held at its tip is one single transparent droplet, water-clear and colourless, catching a bright specular highlight, with a second identical droplet already resting on the cheekbone below it as a small clear domed bead that sits on the skin and lets the pores show straight through it. The fingers holding the tube are relaxed with short natural unpainted nails, and only the fingertips and the first knuckle are in frame. Real skin kept real at this magnification: individual pores, fine down catching the light, natural fine lines, one or two small natural marks, and uneven sheen so some areas read matte and others slightly shiny. The texture never resolves into swirls, whorls, concentric rings or any repeating pattern. One large soft key from the upper left rakes low across the cheek so the skin texture reads, with one dim cool fill on the shadow side. 100mm macro at f5.6, the droplet and the skin around it sharp, the dropper tip falling gently soft, fine film grain, natural skin tones, quiet and expensive.
